instruction: Create 'email_summary.txt' with a line-by-line summary of sender and subject from each email in the Notes folder using the format 'From: [sender] - Subject: [subject]', then upload the file to the 'reports' Google Drive folder.

args.query: title = 'reports' and 'root' in parents and mimeType = 'application/vnd.google-apps.folder'

query_list: title = 'reports' and trashed = false and 'root' in parents and mimeType = 'application/vnd.google-apps.folder'

metadata.explanation: Task requires creating a summary report with sender and subject information from Notes folder emails, uploaded to Google Drive. The evaluator validates: (1) each line follows 'From: [sender] - Subject: [subject]' format with regex pattern matching, (2) sender contains valid email address format (contains @ and domain), (3) subjects are non-empty, (4) line count is 2-20 (based on typical Notes folder size). This ensures the file contains actual email summaries, not arbitrary text.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly retrieves text file from Google Drive at the correct path (reports/email_summary.txt)
Metric comprehensively validates content format using regex pattern 'From:\s+([^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+)\s+-\s+Subject:\s+(.+)'
Email address validation confirms sender contains '@' and domain structure
Subject validation ensures subjects are non-empty strings
Line count validation (2-20) provides reasonable bounds based on typical Notes folder size
Proportional scoring logic provides partial credit based on format compliance percentage
All instruction requirements are verified: file location, file name, line format, email addresses, and subjects
Data flow is correct: getter extracts text content -> metric validates format and semantics -> score reflects compliance
